name: Code the Dream
description: Code the Dream expands access to tech careers for individuals from underrepresented communities through free coding education and paid apprenticeships. By combining training with real-world experience, the program builds skills, creates opportunity, and delivers technology that benefits communities.

name: Student U
description: Student U is a Durham-based nonprofit working to create a more equitable education system by supporting students facing systemic barriers. Through long-term academic and college-access support, Student U helps students reach their full potential.

name: Youth LEAD NC
description: Youth LEAD NC is a nonprofit that empowers individuals with disabilities ages 30 and under through peer support and leadership development, preparing them to succeed in education, employment, independent living, and community leadership.

name: North Carolina Civics Coalition (NC3)
description: The North Carolina Civics Coalition (NC3) is a nonpartisan organization dedicated to strengthening and advancing K–12 civic education across North Carolina.

name: Pasquines Volunteer and Internship Program
description: Pasquines offers flexible volunteer and internship opportunities with a nonprofit news organization covering U.S. territories, allowing participants to build skills through remote, tech-driven collaboration. Requiring as little as two hours per week, it is ideal for students interested in journalism, public administration, political science, and law who want to gain experience while making an impact.

name: Teens In Public Service (TIPS) Internship
description: Teens In Public Service (TIPS) offers paid summer internships that place high school students with nonprofit organizations to make a meaningful impact in their communities. The program helps teens gain real-world experience while developing leadership skills and a strong sense of civic responsibility.

name: Arts Access
description: Arts Access is an organization that supports individuals with disabilities in accessing and participating in the arts. Volunteers can contribute skills in marketing and graphic design to help expand outreach and increase community engagement. It is a meaningful opportunity to support inclusivity while applying creative skills.

name: A Place at the Table
description: This welcoming downtown café builds community by serving fresh, delicious meals to everyone, regardless of their ability to pay. Guests can support others by adding a token to their bill to help cover someone else’s meal. It is a meaningful place to enjoy good food while giving back.

name: Communities in Schools of Wake County
description: This program supports students in staying in school and graduating by connecting them with mentors and community resources. Volunteers can get involved as youth mentors or assist in after school centers to provide guidance and support. It is a meaningful way to help students succeed academically and personally.

name: Designed for Joy
description: This studio on Crabtree Boulevard creates stylish leather earrings while providing meaningful employment for women in transitional situations. It offers a living wage, work experience, and professional references to help participants move forward in the job market. Supporting the studio, in person or online, helps empower women through opportunity and skill building.

name: Dorcas Ministries
description: Dorcas Ministries provides emergency support such as food, clothing, shelter, transportation, and other essential services to those in need. They are currently seeking grocery store gift cards to support clients of their food pantry. Donating is a direct way to help families facing immediate challenges.

name: Families Together
description: Families Together helps families experiencing homelessness secure stable housing and connect with essential community resources. Supporters can get involved by joining the Landlord Network, creating welcome baskets, or providing gifts for families during the holidays. It is a meaningful way to help families rebuild stability and independence.

name: Friends of Wake County Animal Center
description: FWCAC supports animals in the community by funding medical care, organizing supply drives, and facilitating fostering and adoption. Volunteers can contribute by using photography skills for adoption listings or fostering pets during the holidays. It is a meaningful way to improve the lives of animals while supporting their journey to permanent homes.

name: The Green Chair Project
description: Green Chair helps families recovering from homelessness, crisis, or disaster by providing essential home furnishings to create a sense of comfort and stability. Supporters can donate gently used furniture or new, gender neutral twin sized bedding to help furnish homes for those in need. It is a direct way to help local families rebuild and feel at home again.

name: Haven House Services
description: Haven House supports youth experiencing homelessness or crisis through a range of programs, including an emergency shelter for ages 10 to 17. Community members can get involved by adopting a family and providing holiday gifts to brighten a young person’s season. It is a meaningful way to support vulnerable youth and bring comfort during difficult times.

name: Helping Horse
description: This therapeutic riding program provides group lessons for individuals with physical, mental, and emotional needs, helping build coordination and confidence. Supporters can donate new or gently used equipment such as saddles, bridles, and grooming tools. It is a meaningful way to promote healing and empowerment through equine therapy.

name: Inter-Faith Food Shuttle
description: The Food Shuttle works to combat hunger by providing food access and community support programs. Volunteers can lead health education classes, organize food drives, or support initiatives like Backpack Buddies at local schools. It offers multiple ways to make a direct impact on food insecurity in the community.

name: Kid Lab
description: This downtown nonprofit makerspace and community art collective offers pay what you can, play based creative experiences for all ages. Donating art supplies helps expand access and inspire creativity in more kids and families. It is a great way to support inclusive, hands on learning in the community.

name: Lutheran Family Services Resettlement Help
description: LFS supports refugees and immigrants by helping them secure housing, access healthcare, and enroll in school. Community members can join a “Circle of Welcome” or donate essential household items like tea kettles and rice cookers. It is a meaningful way to help families settle in and build a new life.

name: Me Fine Foundation
description: Me Fine supports families with critically ill children by providing financial and emotional assistance so they can focus on their child’s care. Donating gas cards helps families travel to important medical appointments and follow ups. It is a simple but meaningful way to ease both financial and emotional burdens.

name: NC Hunters for the Hungry
description: Licensed hunters can donate legally harvested deer, which are processed at state inspected facilities and turned into nutritious venison for those in need. The program helps manage deer overpopulation in North Carolina while providing high quality protein to people experiencing hunger. It is a unique way to support both environmental balance and food access.

name: Note in the Pocket
description: Note in the Pocket supports children in poverty by providing high quality clothing that helps them feel confident and succeed in school. Donations of new or gently used clothing in sizes 5T through adult help meet the needs of students of all ages. It is a meaningful way to support both dignity and academic success.

name: Oak City Cares
description: This community hub works to make homelessness rare, brief, and non recurring by providing essential services like meals, showers, laundry, medical screenings, and computer access. Volunteers can help by serving meals or assisting at the front desk. It is a direct way to support individuals working toward stability and independence.

name: Oak City Recovery Run Club
description: At OCRRC, the Raleigh running community comes together with individuals in recovery through regular group runs, helping reduce the stigma around addiction. Participants can join 1, 3, or 5 mile runs or donate winter running gear to support the program. It is a powerful way to build community, promote wellness, and support recovery.

name: Raleigh Community Kickstand
description: This bicycle cooperative repairs donated bikes, teaches maintenance skills, and provides bicycles to unhoused neighbors to support reliable transportation. Community members can donate adult sized bikes or offer space for pop up workshops. It is a practical way to promote mobility, skill building, and community support.

name: Read and Feed
description: Read and Feed supports elementary students by combining after school literacy tutoring with nutritious meals. Donating diverse K to 5 books or gas cards helps expand access to their mobile classroom and resources. It is a meaningful way to support both education and food security for children.

name: SAFEChild
description: SAFEChild works to prevent child abuse and support families through education, advocacy, and parent to parent programs. Volunteers can mentor new mothers, lead children’s groups, or donate items from their wish list. It is a meaningful way to strengthen families and create safer environments for children.

name: StepUp Ministry
description: StepUp helps individuals find employment, build life skills, and create stability within a supportive community. Donating large sized professional men’s clothing helps stock their winter closet and prepares participants for job opportunities. It is a practical way to support confidence and long term success.

name: Triangle Land Conservancy
description: TLC works to preserve natural spaces and connect people with nature in a rapidly developing region. Volunteers can help prepare new nature preserves or support efforts by donating vehicles for work days. It is a meaningful way to protect the environment and expand access to outdoor spaces.

name: Urban Ministries
description: Urban Ministries supports individuals facing crisis or poverty by providing food, medicine, and shelter with compassion and dignity. Donations of clothing like T shirts, yoga pants, socks, and underwear help women at the Helen Wright Center meet basic needs. It is a direct way to offer comfort and support during difficult times.
